ranking.note: Raised to P1: complete failure of a shipped tool on a supported platform (Windows wrapper never waits for its child), which the bands list as typical P1.
Raised to P1 for parity with #36105: the installed wrapper fails outright on distros with non-standard libexec paths (#35785), a supported-platform failure.

Raised to P2 and moved up 7: options after a command being silently ignored can direct bitcoin-cli/bitcoin-wallet at the wrong wallet, a correctness hazard across all the CLI tools, not mere ergonomics.
Raised to P2: brings multiprocess tooling to a supported platform, the same class of platform-parity problem as #36105/#36106 but broader and less immediate.
Raised to P2 for consistency with #35831: CLI tools silently operating on a different datadir than the GUI can misplace wallet and block data.
Moved up 7: this is the only PR here touching signing correctness in a key/transaction tool (bitcoin-tx), which the category ranks above developer-productivity scripts.
Moved up 7: seed generation is the first thing this category says matters; a crash in makeseeds during release preparation outranks developer helper scripts even though the fix is small.
Moved down 7: a large speedup, but it only affects an offline fuzz-coverage helper, which the category ranks below tool correctness and seed/wallet tooling.
Moved down 5: internal dependency-check tooling with a real macOS false-pass fix, but below user-facing tool fixes in this category.
Moved up 5: among the niche contrib script fixes it is the clearest crash-with-total-output-loss, so it leads the P4 script group.
Lowered to P4 for consistency with #31888, the other linearize-data.py fix: a reliable hang, but in a niche offline contrib script.
Moved up 5 to sit next to #36157, the other linearize-data.py fix, since the two overlap and should be looked at together.
Lowered to P4: within tools its contribution is a reusable bitcoin-tidy check with speculative payoff, the same treatment given to #35054, whose tools-relevant part is one maintenance script.

inconsistencies: #36105 and #32387 overlap: the Windows exec/child-wait fix appears to be carved out of the larger Windows IPC PR. Review #36105 first; #32387 should then be rebased on it and also depends on upstream libmultiprocess changes.

#36157 and #31888 both modify contrib/linearize/linearize-data.py and will likely conflict. Review #36157 first (one-line, reproducible hang, active author); #31888 has been stalled awaiting the agreed doc updates.

#35608 and #35809 both modify contrib/devtools/deterministic-fuzz-coverage. Review #35608 first (the runtime reduction) so the added coverage_check flag in #35809 is written against the new comparison path.

IPC chain: #19460 sits on top of the multiprocess stack (#29409/#10102) and is the least useful of the IPC tool PRs on its own; #32387 (platform parity) and #30437 (client-side IPC coverage) should be looked at before it.
#35903 may be moot: a reviewer asked whether #35958 makes the non-printable msgtype condition unreachable. Confirm that before spending review time.

#35569 and #35054 are large non-tools projects whose only tools-category footprint is a helper (a tidy check, a Merkle-root script); their real evaluation belongs in the refactor/p2p categories, and their band here reflects only the tooling piece.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: two outright platform failures of the bitcoin wrapper (#36105, #36106) at the top, then a small P2 group where a tool silently acts on the wrong wallet or datadir (#35831, #27409) plus Windows multiprocess parity (#32387). The P3 band is ordered by the category's own priorities: key/transaction-touching tools and seed generation before developer helper scripts. Everything under contrib that is a niche single-purpose script sits in P4 regardless of how real its bug is.
